title: Remove Invalid Parentheses
notes:
Task: Remove the fewest parentheses to make the string valid and return every distinct result.
Idea: BFS over strings formed by deleting one parenthesis per step; stop at the first level with valid strings.
Invariant: Every string in a BFS level has the same number of deletions, so the first successful level is minimal.
Edge cases: Preserve non-parenthesis characters and deduplicate repeated results.
complexity_reason: The BFS can generate exponentially many deletion variants, and validating each string costs O(n).

title: Remove Invalid Parentheses
notes:
Task: Remove the minimum number of parentheses needed to make the string valid.
Idea: Process unique strings level by level, deleting one parenthesis at each transition.
Invariant: BFS levels represent equal deletion counts; the first valid level therefore contains only minimum-deletion answers.
Edge cases: A set avoids duplicate strings; letters are never deleted.
complexity_reason: There can be exponentially many unique strings and each validation or deletion costs linear time.

title: Range Sum Query - Immutable
notes:
Task: Answer inclusive range-sum queries on an array that does not change.
Idea: Store cumulative sums with a leading zero, then subtract prefix[left] from prefix[right+1].
Invariant: prefix[i] equals the sum of the first i values.
Edge cases: The leading zero makes queries starting at index zero use the same formula.
complexity_reason: One prefix value is stored per array position, and each query uses two indexed reads.

title: Range Sum Query - Immutable
notes:
Task: Support repeated inclusive range-sum queries on a fixed array.
Idea: Precompute prefix sums with a zero at index 0, then subtract two prefixes per query.
Invariant: prefix[i] stores the sum of nums[0..i-1].
Edge cases: A query beginning at zero is handled by the sentinel prefix.
complexity_reason: The constructor fills a prefix array and each query performs constant work.

title: Range Sum Query 2D - Immutable
notes:
Task: Answer sums of inclusive rectangular regions in a fixed matrix.
Idea: Build a padded prefix table using inclusion-exclusion; query four corners to recover a rectangle.
Invariant: prefix[r][c] is the sum of matrix cells in rows before r and columns before c.
Edge cases: Padding avoids special cases for rectangles touching the top or left boundary.
complexity_reason: The prefix table stores one value per matrix cell plus a padded border.

title: Range Sum Query 2D - Immutable
notes:
Task: Answer inclusive rectangle-sum queries without rescanning the matrix.
Idea: Precompute a padded two-dimensional prefix sum and use inclusion-exclusion for each query.
Invariant: pref[r][c] covers rows less than r and columns less than c.
Edge cases: The zero border supports queries that begin at row zero or column zero.
complexity_reason: The table is quadratic in matrix dimensions and each query uses four prefix values.

title: Additive Number
notes:
Task: Decide whether a digit string splits into at least three additive-sequence values.
Idea: Enumerate the first two numeric prefixes, then require every next sum to match the remaining text.
Invariant: After choosing two values, every accepted next substring is exactly their sum and becomes the next pair.
Edge cases: Multi-digit values cannot start with zero; values are bounded by signed 32-bit maximum.
code:
class Solution:
    def isAdditiveNumber(self, num: str) -> bool:
        n=len(num); limit=2**31-1
        for i in range(1,n):
            if num[0]=='0' and i>1: break
            a=int(num[:i])
            for j in range(i+1,n):
                if num[i]=='0' and j>i+1: break
                b=int(num[i:j])
                if a>limit or b>limit: break
                pos=j; x,y=a,b; count=2
                while pos<n:
                    z=x+y; text=str(z)
                    if z>limit or not num.startswith(text,pos): break
                    pos+=len(text); x,y=y,z; count+=1
                if pos==n and count>=3: return True
        return False
complexity_reason: There are O(n^2) prefix pairs and each attempted sequence may scan O(n) characters.

title: Additive Number
notes:
Task: Check whether a digit string can form a sequence where each later value is the sum of the prior two.
Idea: Try every legal split for the first two numbers and match generated sums from left to right.
Invariant: The current pair is the last two accepted values, and pos marks the next unconsumed character.
Edge cases: Reject leading zeros in multi-digit numbers and stop when a value exceeds Integer.MAX_VALUE.
complexity_reason: There are O(n^2) first-pair splits, and matching sums may scan the remaining string.

title: Range Sum Query - Mutable
notes:
Task: Support point updates and inclusive range-sum queries on a mutable array.
Idea: Store values in a Fenwick tree; update propagates along parent indices and prefix queries jump backward by low bits.
Invariant: tree nodes store partial sums covering ranges determined by their least significant set bit.
Edge cases: The implementation keeps a copy of values so updates can compute the delta.
time_complexity: O(n log n) construction; O(log n) update/query
complexity_reason: Each Fenwick operation visits logarithmically many indices.

title: Range Sum Query - Mutable
notes:
Task: Design a mutable array with point updates and inclusive range sums.
Idea: Use a Fenwick tree for logarithmic point updates and prefix sums, subtracting prefixes for a range.
Invariant: bit[i] stores the sum of the interval ending at i whose length is its low bit.
Edge cases: Keep the current values to calculate the delta for each update.
time_complexity: O(n log n) construction; O(log n) update/query
complexity_reason: Fenwick updates and prefix queries traverse O(log n) tree indices.

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock with Cooldown
notes:
Task: Maximize profit with unlimited transactions and one cooldown day after selling.
Idea: Track holding, sold today, and resting states; buying is allowed only from the prior resting state.
Invariant: Each state is the best profit after processing the current day with that exact trading status.
Edge cases: Empty and one-day price lists yield zero profit.
complexity_reason: Each day performs constant state transitions and stores three values.

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock with Cooldown
notes:
Task: Find maximum stock profit when selling prevents buying on the next day.
Idea: Maintain the best holding, sold-today, and resting profits as daily states.
Invariant: hold, sold, and rest describe mutually exclusive statuses after the processed prefix.
Edge cases: Initialize holding as unreachable and return zero for an empty list.
complexity_reason: The single pass updates a fixed number of state variables per price.

title: Minimum Height Trees
notes:
Task: Return the tree roots that minimize its height.
Idea: Repeatedly remove all current degree-one leaves until at most two vertices remain.
Invariant: Remaining vertices form the central tree after equal-distance outer layers have been stripped.
Edge cases: A one-node tree returns [0]; a two-node tree returns both vertices.
complexity_reason: Each vertex and edge is removed at most once from the adjacency structure.

title: Minimum Height Trees
notes:
Task: Find every root that yields a minimum-height rooted tree.
Idea: Queue all leaves and peel complete layers until one or two central nodes remain.
Invariant: Removing a leaf layer preserves the tree's center as the center of the remaining tree.
Edge cases: Handle n<=2 directly; a tree with n vertices has n-1 edges.
complexity_reason: Adjacency sets hold O(n) tree edges and each leaf is removed once.

title: Burst Balloons
notes:
Task: Maximize coins earned by bursting balloons, where each reward uses the current neighboring values.
Idea: Add boundary ones and choose the last balloon burst in each interval.
Invariant: dp[left][right] is the best score for bursting balloons strictly between the two boundary indices.
Edge cases: Empty input returns zero; the padded ones simplify intervals touching either end.
complexity_reason: There are O(n^2) intervals and each tries every possible last balloon.

title: Burst Balloons
notes:
Task: Maximize the total coin reward from bursting all balloons in an optimal order.
Idea: Pad the values with ones and fill interval DP by increasing interval length.
Invariant: dp[l][r] is the maximum reward for the balloons between boundary balloons l-1 and r+1.
Edge cases: An empty input returns zero; shorter intervals are already computed before larger ones.
complexity_reason: The interval table has O(n^2) entries and each entry examines O(n) last-burst choices.

title: Super Ugly Number
notes:
Task: Return the nth positive number whose prime factors come only from primes.
Idea: Maintain a candidate product for each prime and append the smallest candidate at each step.
Invariant: dp contains the increasing sequence of generated super ugly numbers, and each pointer references a valid prior term.
Edge cases: Advance every pointer whose product equals the chosen minimum to avoid duplicates.
complexity_reason: For each of n outputs, the algorithm scans p prime candidates and stores the sequence plus pointer arrays.

title: Super Ugly Number
notes:
Task: Find the nth positive integer whose prime divisors all belong to the given list.
Idea: Generate numbers in order from prime-times-earlier-number candidates.
Invariant: dp[0..i] is the increasing sequence generated so far, and each pointer identifies the next factor product for its prime.
Edge cases: Advance all tied candidates so the output sequence contains no duplicate values.
complexity_reason: Each generated number scans all p candidate products and stores n sequence values and p pointers.

title: Count of Smaller Numbers After Self
notes:
Task: Count, for every element, the strictly smaller values to its right.
Idea: Merge-sort index pairs; when a right-half value is smaller, count it before the left item.
Invariant: Each recursive half is sorted, and moved right-half elements are smaller than the current left item.
Edge cases: Equal values are not counted as smaller; original indices preserve answer positions.
complexity_reason: Merge sort performs O(log n) levels with linear merge work per level.

title: Count of Smaller Numbers After Self
notes:
Task: For each value, count strictly smaller values located to its right.
Idea: Merge-sort index/value pairs and accumulate how many right-half elements have passed each left-half element.
Invariant: Recursive halves are sorted; the moved-right counter counts right-side values strictly smaller than the current left value.
Edge cases: Equal values are merged from the left first, so they are not counted as smaller.
complexity_reason: Each merge level processes every index once, with logarithmically many levels.
